rows.note: Use this colloquial shorthand for an explosion, especially in casual references to blasting or demolition.

example.english: We need a blast to demolish that rock wall.
example.jyutping: caak3 go2 fuk1 sek6 coeng4 jiu3 jung6 baau3

rows.note: Use this when playing music or a recording at a very high volume; it is the natural everyday choice for that context.

example.english: We blast the music so loudly that the whole building can hear it.
example.traditional: 我哋播到好大聲，成棟樓都聽到。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 bo3 dou3 hou2 daai6 seng1 sing4 dung6 lau4 dou1 teng1 dou2

rows.note: Use this for blasting or blowing a hole right through a wall or other solid object.

example.english: We used explosives to blast a hole through the wall.
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 jung6 zaa3 joek6 zaa3 cyun1 dou6 coeng4

rows.note: Use this for a bout of severe scolding or verbal attack directed at someone.

example.english: Mum gave me a blast yesterday.
example.traditional: 阿媽尋日畀咗我一輪鬧。
example.jyutping: aa3 maa1 cam4 jat6 bei2 zo2 ngo5 jat1 leon4 naau6

rows.note: Use this colloquially when severely criticizing or publicly attacking someone or something with words.

example.traditional: 網民喺網上鬧爆間公司。
example.jyutping: mong5 man4 hai2 mong5 soeng6 naau6 baau3 gaan1 gung1 si1

rows.note: Use this all-purpose noun phrase for a sudden gust of wind.

example.english: A blast of wind just blew the paper away.
example.traditional: 啱啱一陣風，吹到張紙飛走咗。
example.jyutping: ngaam1 ngaam1 jat1 zan6 fung1 ceoi1 dou3 zoeng1 zi2 fei1 zau2 zo2

rows.note: Use this for the loud, sudden sound itself, especially when describing a bang or report.

example.traditional: 突然一聲巨響，嚇親我哋。
example.jyutping: dat6 jin4 jat1 seng1 geoi6 hoeng2 haak3 can1 ngo5 dei6

rows.note: Use this when the shooting involves firearms, especially shooting at a person or place.

example.english: They blast at the police from the rooftop.
example.traditional: 佢哋喺天台向警察開槍。
example.jyutping: keoi5 dei6 hai2 tin1 toi4 hoeng3 ging2 caat3 hoi1 coeng1
